cards.text: Ezekiel the prophet is still in his vision of the new temple, and the LORD is still speaking. Now He gets to the land. When it's divided up by lot as an inheritance, one portion has to be set aside.

cards.question: When the land is divided up by lot, who gets a portion set aside?

cards.text: And this is no little garden patch. It's 25,000 cubits long and 20,000 wide, and friend, I spent YEARS in the back of a junk drawer, so I don't even know what to DO with that much room.

cards.question: Only part of the LORD's portion of land is holy, and the rest is ordinary land.

cards.text: Inside that area, the sanctuary gets a square 500 cubits on each side, with 50 cubits of open land around it. Then a strip 25,000 by 10,000 is measured off, and the sanctuary, the Most Holy Place, will be in it.

cards.question: Who gets to use that holy strip with the sanctuary in it?

answers.text: The priests who minister in the sanctuary
The elders who lead the tribes
The prophets who speak for the LORD

cards.text: That strip is also a place for the priests' houses, right alongside the holy area for the sanctuary. And right next door is another strip, the same size: 25,000 by 10,000.

cards.question: Who gets the strip right beside the priests' land?

answers.text: The Levites who minister in the temple
The judges who rule over the tribes
The soldiers who guard the king

cards.text: The Levites get it as their possession, for towns to live in. Then one more strip, 5,000 wide and 25,000 long, is set aside beside the holy district as the city's property.

cards.question: The city's land belongs to the whole house of Israel.

cards.text: Now the prince, the leader of Israel in this vision, gets the land on both sides of the holy district and the city's property, stretching west and east. It will be his possession in Israel.

cards.question: Once the prince has his own land, he also gets to keep the rest of the land for himself.
God says His princes will no longer ___ His people, but will give the rest of the land to the house of Israel by tribes.

cards.text: Then the Lord GOD speaks straight to the princes: "Enough, O princes of Israel! Cease your violence and oppression…"

cards.question: Instead of violence and oppression, what does God tell the princes of Israel to do?

answers.text: Do what is just and right
Build up the walls of the city
Gather more land for the temple

cards.text: He tells them to stop dispossessing His people. Then God turns to everyday business: how weighing and measuring is done.

cards.question: Next, God says to use ___ scales, along with a just ephah and a just bath.

cards.text: Then He sets one standard for every measure and weight, right down to the shekel and the mina. Somewhere, every measuring cup in Israel just stood up a little straighter.

Next comes the contribution: a share of the wheat, the barley, the oil, and even one sheep from every flock of two hundred. One sheep out of two hundred is math I can HANDLE, friend, because back in that junk drawer, my big night out was counting the dust as it fell.

cards.question: This contribution is for the prince in Israel. Who has to take part in it?

answers.text: All the people of the land
Only the elders of the tribes

cards.question: The people bring their contribution to the prince. So what is the prince's part?

answers.text: Provide the offerings for the feasts
Build a palace beside the temple
Pay the priests their yearly wages

cards.question: The offerings the prince provides are to make atonement for the house of Israel.

cards.text: Then the Lord GOD gives dates to keep, starting with the first day of the first month.

cards.question: On the first day of the first month, a young bull without blemish is taken. What is it for?

cards.text: The priest puts some of the blood from that sin offering on the temple doorposts, the corners of the altar's ledge and the inner court's gateposts. And on the seventh day of the month, the same thing is done again.

cards.question: The seventh-day offering is only for people who stray on purpose.

cards.text: It's for anyone who strays unintentionally or in ignorance, and that's how atonement is made for the temple. Friend, I once stamped a WHOLE batch upside down and didn't find out till they were cooling.
Then, on the fourteenth day of the first month, comes the Passover, a feast of seven days with unleavened bread.

cards.question: On the day of the Passover, the prince provides a bull as a sin offering for himself and for all the ___ of the land.

cards.text: Then, each of the seven days of the feast, he provides seven bulls and seven rams without blemish as a burnt offering to the LORD, plus a male goat for a sin offering.
On top of that comes a grain offering: an ephah for each bull and each ram, with a hin of olive oil for each ephah. That's fourteen ephahs a day, friend, and my oven just started SWEATING.
Then, later in the year, there's another seven-day feast. It begins on the fifteenth day of the seventh month.

cards.question: For the seven-day feast in the seventh month, what does the prince provide?

answers.text: The same offerings as at Passover
Twice as many offerings as at Passover
Only the grain offerings and oil

cards.text: And that's where we'll pause for now, friend. This vision's not done yet, so keep that apron on.
